stories.title: C.J. Stroud connects with Nico Collins to give Texans 7-3 lead
stories.summary: The Texans were outplayed for most of the first quarter, but they have a 7-3 lead.
stories.detail: The Texans were outplayed for most of the first quarter, but they have a 7-3 lead. Spencer Shrader kicked a 34-yard field but missed from 56, giving the Colts an early 3-0 lead. They had drives of nine plays, 44 yards and eight plays, 35 yards. The Colts defense, missing cornerbacks Charvarius Ward and Sauce Gardner, intercepted C.J. Stroud on the Texans' first drive. It was a fluke pick, first hitting AJ Haulcy in the helmet, then off the hands of Cam Bynum before landing back in Haulcy's hands. The Texans, though, answered on their second drive. Stroud avoided the blitz of cornerback Kapena Gushiken, who grabbed a piece of Stroud's jersey, by stepping up in the pocket before heaving a dime into the end zone to Nico Collins. Collins was covered by Justin Walley, but it was no match. The 42-yard touchdown pass gave the Texans their first lead. It was Stroud's 20th touchdown. His career high is 23.

stories.title: Texans lose Chris Braswell to serious-looking knee injury
stories.summary: Texans defensive end Chris Braswell suffered a serious-looking knee injury on the opening kickoff of Thursday night's game against the Colts.
stories.detail: HOUSTON -- Texans defensive end Chris Braswell suffered a serious-looking knee injury on the opening kickoff of Thursday night's game against the Indianapolis Colts . As the ball was being returned by the Colts, Braswell collided with Indianapolis defensive end Caden Curry and his leg buckled, sending him down to the ground immediately. A medical cart came out for Braswell, and payers surrounded him while an air cast was placed on his right leg. The 25-year-old, a second-round pick of Tampa Bay in 2024 after playing at Alabama, had his head in his hands and a towel covering his face as he was driven off the field. The Texans ruled him out shortly after. Thursday night was Braswell's first time playing in a Texans uniform after landing on their practice squad Sept. 1. He was promoted to the active roster earlier in the offseason before being waived and returning to the practice squad. He was elevated to the active roster ahead of Thursday night's game.

stories.title: Texans DE Chris Braswell seriously injures leg on opening kickoff
stories.summary: Texans defensive end Chris Braswell was seriously injured on the opening kickoff.
stories.detail: Texans defensive end Chris Braswell was seriously injured on the opening kickoff. Braswell, who was elevated from the practice squad for the game, injured his right leg on what appeared to be a blindside block by Caden Curry. No penalty was called on Seth McGown's 40-yard return. The team's medical personnel placed his right leg in a vacuum splint before he was carted to the training room. Braswell's teammates wished him well before he departed on a cart. The Texans immediately ruled him out. It was the first play of the first game Braswell has played this season. A second-round pick of the Bucs in 2024, he had played all 34 games in his first two seasons.

teamStories.detail: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images In terms of accountability, the Las Vegas Raiders have that locked down at the all-important head coach and quarterback spot with Klint Kubiak and Fernando Mendoza, respectively. stories.detail: MINNEAPOLIS — In his own words, this should be an uncomfortable situation for Karl-Anthony Towns. Regardless, it’s produced some of the best basketball of his career . Before the season, when Towns still was publicly pushing for a contract extension from the Knicks, he said he wanted his long-term future settled “so I can feel as comfortable as possible.” Without a new deal, he said, “there’s no comfortability to be had.” Karl-Anthony Towns rises up for a rebound during the Knicks’ win over the Raptors on Nov. 17, 2026, in Toronto. NBAE via Getty Images That new deal, of course, never materialized, as the Knicks shut down all extension negotiations for the season while navigating owner James Dolan’s mandate to stay under the second apron. It left Towns in that uncomfortable situation. Fans will be able to indulge in the limited-edition offering of creamy peanut butter and grape jelly on white sourdough bread -- Flagg's preferred combination. They are set to be priced at $3.20, a nod to Flagg's No. 32, with just 320 sandwiches supplied and given out in a sandwich bag sealed with a sticker. They are available while supplies last on the American Airlines Center's main plaza level outside section 117. teamStories.title: Sources: Spurs' Dylan Harper out 1-3 weeks with hip strain
teamStories.summary: Spurs guard Dylan Harper has been diagnosed with a left hip rotator strain, avoiding any major injury, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Thursday.
teamStories.detail: San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper has been diagnosed with a left hip rotator strain, avoiding any major injury, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Thursday. This type of strain will carry a one-to-three-week timetable for return, dependent on Harper's rehab. Harper was injured when he appeared to slip on a wet spot in the team's 105-93 loss to the Detroit Pistons in San Antonio on Tuesday night. Harper writhed on the floor in pain after the play and appeared to grab at his groin area. "The visuals and optics of falls, potential injuries, whatever you want to call it can be impressionable. And that one did not look great," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said. "So, there's a lot of WebMD and you try not to let your mind run the wrong way and you hope for the best," he continued. "But you really don't know. It's part of the things we can't control. So, we're just very lucky, fortunate and mostly just happy for Dylan that there will be some time [that he's out]. Very best case scenario for a lot of the things that could have been."
